title: Finite Test Pit, Dual Tyres and Interlayer Bonding: A Verified Three-Dimensional Finite Element Analysis of a Circular Accelerated Pavement Testing Facility
content: Circular accelerated pavement testing (APT) facilities are usually interpreted with linear elastic layered theory (LET), which ignores the finite test pit and the dual wheel and requires an interface assumption. This study quantifies these effects for the ALT-LIRA facility (Iași, Romania), a ring track in a 1.8 m deep concrete pit loaded by a 57.5 kN dual wheel. A three-dimensional finite element (FE) model of the reference sector was verified against Alizé-LCPC and a large-domain model, and compared with strains, pressures and Benkelman deflections measured over 106 passes. The FE model reproduced the LET asphalt strain within 1% and the subgrade strain within 3%, whereas the rigid pit reduced the surface deflection by 23% relative to the large domain and by 29% relative to LET. The dual tyres lowered the peak asphalt strain by 6%, and interface sliding increased it by up to 94%. A loss of asphalt stiffness limited to 50% (EN 12697-24) changed the deflection by up to 14% and the asphalt strain by less than 10%, so that it explains only part of the measured growth; with partial friction (μ = 0.5) the model came within 8% of one gauge and 7% of the deflection. Deflection-based back-calculation in APT pits requires the pit geometry and an explicit interface model.
